china-1914:p0545_1.rationale: Protestant mission schools and scholars, plus church congregations and Christian community totals.

china-1914:p0545_2.rationale: Christian mission hospitals, dispensaries and patients, plus Chinese contributions.

china-1914:p0661_1.rationale: Textual list of the hereditary ranks of Mongolian chieftains and their titles. The table concerns official status and has no quantities.
review_questions: Should honours-and-ranks apply to hereditary noble ranks?

china-1914:p0662_1.rationale: Lists Mongolian leagues, banners, chieftain ranks, names and succession dates. Banners are local governing units. The dates are incidental, so the content is textual.
review_questions: Should a banner-specific or honours-and-ranks tag be used?

china-1914:p0664_1.rationale: Roster of Mongol chieftains with rank, name and date of succession. Textual office-holder list.
review_questions: Is a tag for hereditary nobility or office-holders needed?

china-1914:p0664_2.rationale: Lists Outer Mongol Khalkha banners by aimak (tribal unit), giving the banners' organisational positions; textual territorial units with no quantities.

china-1914:p0665_1.rationale: Lists Mongol chieftains with rank, name and succession year. Dates and ranks are incidental, so the content is textual. Hereditary nobility and office-holders fit no precise tag: government-offices is for civil-service posts and honours-and-ranks for decorations.
review_questions: Propose a tag for hereditary native nobility or chieftains of Mongol banners.

china-1914:p0665_2.rationale: Textual list of Tsetsen Khan and Jasaktu Khan aimak banners by guard and wing, i.e. territorial/tribal units; no quantities.

china-1914:p0666_1.rationale: Lists banners of the Jasaktu Khan and Sain Noin aimaks and other tribes with chieftain rank, name and succession date. The content is textual and the dates are incidental. Hereditary chieftains fit no existing tag precisely.
review_questions: Propose a tag for hereditary Mongol chieftains and banner nobility.

china-1914:p0669_1.rationale: Lists Ili tribe chieftains with rank, name and succession year, with a footnote on promotions for loyalty to the Republic. The content is textual; no existing tag fits.
review_questions: Propose a tag for hereditary Mongol chieftains and banner nobility.

china-1914:p0669_2.rationale: Lists banners by tribe under the Tartar General of Ili and other Chinese officials; textual jurisdictional organisation. The rank column is unreadable, so it adds no quantities.

china-1914:p0670_1.rationale: Counts Begs (native officials) by class at each Sinkiang centre, with totals; this is a statistical breakdown of administrative personnel by rank.

china-1914:p0681_1.rationale: Foreign firms and resident persons in China by nationality, with totals, from the Customs returns.
review_questions: Consider overseas-communities for foreign residents in China.

china-1914:p0684_1.rationale: Foreign population of the Shanghai International Settlement by nationality in the 1910 census; it is both demographic and a foreign concession.

china-1914:p0684_2.rationale: Roster of foreign envoys and ministers accredited to Peking in 1913 by seniority, plus chargés d'affaires; textual list of diplomatic personnel with appointment years.

china-1914:p0685_1.rationale: Roster of British consular officers by port, rank, name and appointment date; the content is textual. Consular service fits diplomatic-service. Informal-imperialism is supported by the Shanghai Supreme Court and Mixed Court posts, which imply consular jurisdiction, but this is not stated explicitly.

china-1914:p0687_1.rationale: Lists British consular posts and their districts as marriage officers under the Foreign Marriage Act and China Order in Council. The content is textual and shows consular legal authority over British subjects, so extraterritoriality fits. Consular posts support diplomatic-service.

china-1914:p0699_1.rationale: Roster of foreign staff in the Chinese postal service, with names, ranks, ports and remarks. The content is textual personnel data, not statistics.

china-1914:p0706_1.rationale: Shanghai Volunteer Corps officers by unit and nationality. The figures are unreadable, but the structure shows a numeric table. Military is the main subject, and the nationality breakdown is substantial. Informal-imperialism rests on the foreign settlement defence force.
review_questions: Should a tag for volunteer or municipal defence forces be added? Army is not clearly confirmed for this corps.

china-1914:p0736_1.rationale: Annual net imports of foreign opium into China in piculs, 1863-1912.

china-1914:p0736_2.rationale: Decadal average annual opium importation in piculs.

china-1914:p0736_3.rationale: Average net weight per chest of each kind of opium, used to measure import figures. It is a weights and units table.

china-1914:p0737_1.rationale: Annual duty, likin and total revenue on foreign opium, 1887-1912.

china-1914:p0737_2.rationale: Duty and likin collected on native opium and duty on foreign opium, by year.

china-1914:p0738_1.rationale: Net imports of foreign opium into Shanghai by type, in pounds and pounds sterling, 1906-12.

china-1914:p0739_1.rationale: Yearly Shanghai prices per picul of foreign opium varieties (Malwa, Patna, Benares, Persian, Turkey, boiled), 1868-1912. These are observed market prices of an opium commodity.

china-1914:p0740_1.rationale: Annual values of native opium by province plus boiled opium, 1869-1893, in Hk. taels. These are observed price or value series for opium.

china-1914:p0741_1.rationale: Continuation of provincial native and boiled opium values in taels, 1894-1912. Many cells are unreadable, but the structure shows a quantitative price series.

china-1914:p0741_2.rationale: Average values of native opium by province and year, 1894-1912, with a Customs Commissioner's note on adulteration. Several cells are unreadable, but the table is a price series.

china-1914:p0744_1.rationale: Sash and ribbon colours for the nine grades of the Chiaoho civil honour. The content is a textual description of insignia, with grade ordinals only.

china-1914:p0746_1.rationale: Counts of foreign and Chinese newspapers registered for transmission through the Chinese Post Office at 20 centres. The subject is newspaper numbers, with the postal channel as context.

china-1914:p0758_1.rationale: Import duty schedule by article with tariff unit and rates, from the 1902 tariff.

china-1914:p0759_1.rationale: Continuation of the customs tariff, with units and duty rates per article.

china-1914:p0760_1.rationale: Continuation of the customs tariff covering printed matter, chemicals, candles, canes and canned foods, with duty rates.

china-1914:p0761_1.rationale: Continuation of the customs tariff for preserved and canned foods, with duty rates by unit.

china-1914:p0762_1.rationale: Schedule of import duty rates per tariff unit for articles from canned meats to cigarettes; rates and rules of customs duties fit tariffs.

china-1914:p0763_1.rationale: Continuation of the customs tariff, listing import duty rates per unit for articles from cigarettes to cotton piece goods.

china-1914:p0764_1.rationale: Customs tariff duty rates for cotton piece goods (drills, jeans, crape and similar) by size and unit.

china-1914:p0765_1.rationale: Tariff duty rates on printed and coloured cotton piece goods by dimensions and unit.

china-1914:p0766_1.rationale: Two-page customs tariff continuation: duty rates for dyed cottons, flannelettes, crimp cloth and velvets.

china-1914:p0768_1.rationale: Customs tariff duty rates for cotton goods, thread and yarn, and dyes and paints.

china-1914:p0769_1.rationale: Customs tariff duty rates for dyes, paints, ivory, enamelware, fans and feathers.

china-1914:p0770_1.rationale: Customs tariff duty rates for articles from files to gum arabic, including fish, ginseng and glass.

china-1914:p0771_1.rationale: Customs tariff duty rates for articles from gum benjamin to lace, including hides, horns and india-rubber.

china-1914:p0772_1.rationale: Customs tariff duty rates for articles from lace to margarine, including leather and lamps.

china-1914:p0773_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates per unit for matches, mats, meats and metals.

china-1914:p0774_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for iron, steel and other metals, with miscellaneous articles.

china-1914:p0776_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for oils, paper, plushes and other articles; opium appears only as one row among many.

china-1914:p0777_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for articles from pork rind to shells.

china-1914:p0778_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for boots, silk goods, soap, soda and sugar.

china-1914:p0779_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for sugar, thread, timber, tobacco and tools.

china-1914:p0780_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for files, umbrellas, wax and sparkling wines.

china-1914:p0781_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for wines, spirits, beers and woods.

china-1914:p0782_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for woods and woollen and cotton mixtures and woollen manufactures.

china-1914:p0783_1.rationale: Customs tariff schedule of duty rates for woollens, yarns and related articles.

china-1919:p0027_1.rationale: Area in square miles of Chinese territorial divisions (China Proper, Mongolia, Turkestan, Tibet).

china-1919:p0028_1.rationale: Census family counts by division of the Empire.

china-1919:p0028_2.rationale: Estimated population by division with a national total.

china-1919:p0028_3.rationale: Series of estimated total population of China at various historical dates.

china-1919:p0029_1.rationale: Provincial area, census and estimated populations, and density; provincial capitals are incidental.

china-1919:p0030_1.rationale: Compares area and population of China and other large countries.

china-1919:p0030_2.rationale: Matrix of nautical-mile distances between ports for shipping reference; no existing tag fits a distance table.
review_questions: Propose a 'distances' tag for route and distance tables.

china-1919:p0030_3.rationale: Overland and rail distances via Siberia between cities; this is a distance matrix, not traffic or railway operating data.
review_questions: Propose a 'distances' tag for route and distance tables.

china-1919:p0030_4.rationale: Coastal sea distances among China coast ports; a distance matrix with no fitting tag.
review_questions: Propose a 'distances' tag for route and distance tables.

china-1919:p0031_1.rationale: Sea distances between Shanghai and northern ports in a stepped matrix; no fitting tag.
review_questions: Propose a 'distances' tag for route and distance tables.

china-1919:p0031_2.rationale: Matrix of river distances in miles between Yangtze ports from Shanghai to Chungking; describes the river's extent as geographical knowledge, not traffic or freight.

china-1919:p0031_3.rationale: Sea distances in miles from Shanghai to northern Chinese, Russian and Japanese ports. This is general geographic distance data, and no existing tag fits route distances.
review_questions: Consider a vocabulary term for distances between places.

china-1919:p0034_1.rationale: Lists the Tienshan chain's ranges with peak heights, which are natural landforms.

china-1919:p0034_2.rationale: Lists Kuenlun chain ranges with approximate heights, which are natural landforms.

china-1919:p0037_1.rationale: Annual highest water-marks of the Yangtze at Hankow since 1865, describing the river's water regime. It is not framed as a flood event table.

china-1919:p0046_1.rationale: Three shark varieties with their lengths, drawn from a Chinese catalogue; a natural species inventory.

china-1919:p0052_1.rationale: Monthly and yearly mean barometric pressure at six stations; a climate observation.

china-1919:p0052_2.rationale: Monthly average rainfall for Shanghai and Hongkong with maxima; a climate observation.

china-1919:p0052_3.rationale: Annual maximum temperatures at Shanghai 1873-1913; a climate observation.

china-1919:p0053_1.rationale: Monthly mean temperatures and humidity for Shanghai and Hongkong; a climate observation.

china-1919:p0053_2.rationale: Maximum number of snow days by month at Sicawei Observatory, Shanghai; these are climate observations.

china-1919:p0053_3.rationale: Prevailing monthly wind direction at Shanghai and Hongkong; these are climate observations.

china-1919:p0054_1.rationale: Monthly barometer, temperature, humidity and rainfall readings for Shanghai in 1910, with departures from average.

china-1919:p0055_1.rationale: Monthly barometer, temperature and rain/snow readings at Weihaiwei for 1910, with annual means and totals.

china-1919:p0056_1.rationale: Textual classification of races of the Chinese Empire by group, tribe and habitat; it contains no quantities. Population is the topic and ethnic classification the tag.

china-1919:p0057_1.rationale: Textual list of Turki-family races and their locations, with no quantities. It is an ethnic classification.

china-1919:p0057_2.rationale: Textual list of Tibetan-speaking Mongoloid races and their districts, with no quantities. It is an ethnic classification.

china-1919:p0057_3.rationale: Textual list of Chinese isolating-speech races (Punti, Hakka and others) and their locations. It is an ethnic classification with no quantities.

china-1919:p0057_4.rationale: Textual list of highland races of undetermined affinity (Miaotze group, Lolo and others) with their locations. It is an ethnic classification with no quantities. The source does not frame these groups as indigenous peoples.

china-1919:p0060_1.rationale: List of Manchu dynasty rulers with reign years; this is a textual roster in which the dates are only identifiers.
review_questions: Should there be a tag for dynastic rulers or reign lists? The imperial-household tag concerns the court and royal family, and historical-chronologies concerns event tables.

china-1919:p0063_1.rationale: Official estimate of Chinese living abroad by country with total; the subject is overseas Chinese communities.

china-1919:p0065_1.rationale: Chief Chinese products ranked by export value in sterling for 1913 and 1916; multi-commodity export table.

china-1919:p0067_1.rationale: Textual list of principal products with provinces of origin across animal products, fibres, metals, seeds and timber. No quantities. No aggregate tag fits a multi-sector origin list.
review_questions: Propose a tag for product geography or regional product origins.

china-1919:p0069_1.rationale: Textual list of products by province with export ports and remarks. No statistics. The subject is commodity origins and export ports across many sectors.
review_questions: Propose a tag for regional commodity origins and export routes.

china-1919:p0076_1.rationale: Percentage shares of the world's raw silk trade by country and region, 1911-1916.

china-1919:p0077_1.rationale: Silk export specifications by type with share of total value and chief export ports in 1917.

china-1919:p0078_1.rationale: Annual value of silk exports from China, 1913-17, in Hk. Tls. and sterling.

china-1919:p0079_1.rationale: Annual quantities and values of beans, beancake and bean oil, 1911-1917, described as the soya bean trade.
review_questions: The table does not state whether the figures are exports; verify the trade direction.

china-1919:p0084_1.rationale: Yarn deliveries in Shanghai by origin (Shanghai, Japanese, Indian), 1913-1914.
review_questions: Is cotton yarn explicit enough to add the cotton tag?

china-1919:p0085_1.rationale: Annual wood-oil exports in pounds, 1912-1916; wood oil is tung oil.

china-1919:p0085_2.rationale: Original export of tobacco from Customs districts in pounds, 1913-1917; an export trade series for tobacco.

china-1919:p0085_3.rationale: Tonnage of abutilon, hemp, jute and ramie moving through the Customs; these are raw vegetable fibres and the table records trade movement.

china-1919:p0086_1.rationale: Ground-nut exports in tons, 1911-1917. Groundnuts are oilseeds.

china-1919:p0086_2.rationale: Camphor exports in pounds, 1907-1917; export trade in a forest product.

china-1919:p0087_1.rationale: Medicinal materials of Szechuan with prices per 100 lb and annual quantities available, listed by the Chamber of Commerce. Mixed prices and quantities, so statistical.
review_questions: Vocabulary lacks a tag for medicinal herbs or materials as commodities; consider proposing one.

china-1919:p0087_2.rationale: Strawbraid export amounts in cwt and values, 1910-1913; no specific tag for strawbraid, a peasant handicraft product.
review_questions: Strawbraid has no dedicated tag; consider proposing one (straw plaiting).

china-1919:p0088_1.rationale: Continuation table of export amount in cwt and value for 1914-1917. The commodity is not identified in the table itself.
review_questions: Commodity not named in the record; it is likely strawbraid continuing from the previous page.

china-1919:p0088_2.rationale: Percentage shares of France, Great Britain, the United States and Japan in an export trade, 1910-1917; exports by destination.
review_questions: Commodity not identified in the table.
Vermicelli has no dedicated tag; food-processing could apply but the table is a trade series.

china-1919:p0088_4.rationale: Customs movement of brown and white sugar in cwt, 1912-1917; sugar commodity trade.

china-1919:p0088_5.rationale: Single row of flour movement through Customs stations in cwt, 1912-1917; context links to the wheat trade. Flour is a traded commodity, but no vocabulary tag covers flour specifically (wheat is a crop/commodity tag, but flour milling is excluded; food-processing is not evidenced).
review_questions: Should a flour or flour-milling tag be added?

china-1919:p0089_1.rationale: Multi-mineral table of acreage, 1914 production and proprietors for coal, iron, tin, antimony, gold, silver, lead, copper and others; an aggregate mineral-production summary.

china-1919:p0090_1.rationale: Estimated coal production by province, divided by coal grade (anthracite, bituminous, lignite).

china-1919:p0090_2.rationale: Estimates of Manchurian coal output by colliery, comparing Kato's 1910 estimate with the Chinese official 1914 estimate.

china-1919:p0091_1.rationale: Comparison of two estimates of coal output by province and mine, with grand totals.

china-1919:p0092_1.rationale: Output in tons of the principal modern collieries in China, 1915.

china-1919:p0093_1.rationale: Annual coal output of the Fushun colliery, April 1909 to March 1918.

china-1919:p0106_1.rationale: Yearly export of antimony products (regulus, crude, ore, ash) from Changsha, 1913-1917 in tons; a commodity export series.

china-1919:p0110_1.rationale: Ladder of theoretical Chinese money units (hao, cash, candareen, mace, tael, cent, dollar) as unit equivalences. Content is a conversion list rather than observed quantities.

china-1919:p0111_1.rationale: Exchange values between different kinds of tael (Haikuan, Kuping, Tientsin, Shanghai), giving numerical equivalences of monetary units rather than currency-market quotations.
review_questions: Is foreign-exchange or currency a better tag for tael-to-tael equivalences?

china-1919:p0112_1.rationale: Equivalence table of standard Chinese units of length, area, capacity and weight against metric and English units; this is a measurement-standards table.

china-1919:p0112_2.rationale: Chain of traditional Chinese weight units from li to picul; a measurement-systems table.

china-1919:p0112_3.rationale: Gives the liang, catty and picul fixed for foreign trade, with grain, pound and metric equivalents. It is a measurement standard for trade use.

china-1919:p0112_4.rationale: Traditional Chinese length units from fên to li, shown as successive equivalents.

china-1919:p0112_5.rationale: States the fixed length of the ch'ih for foreign Customs trade in inches and metres; it is a measurement standard for Customs use.

china-1919:p0113_1.rationale: Compares the length of the ch'ih in inches as used by different trades; a measurement standards table.

china-1919:p0113_2.rationale: Chinese area units with successive equivalents from ssu to ch'ing.

china-1919:p0113_3.rationale: Square ch'ih, pu, mow and ch'ing equivalents for land measurement; a unit-conversion table.

china-1919:p0113_4.rationale: Chinese dry measures of capacity from ko to shih, shown as successive equivalents.

china-1919:p0115_1.rationale: Lists albumen factories with their locations. The content is textual with no quantities, so it is a text table. No existing tag covers albumen or egg-product manufacture.
review_questions: Propose a tag for egg products or albumen manufacture?

china-1919:p0115_2.rationale: Lists locations of Government arsenals in China; purely textual place list; arsenals are military production facilities.

china-1919:p0115_3.rationale: Textual list of canning factories and their locations.

china-1919:p0115_4.rationale: List of cement, brick and tile works with locations; one capacity figure and brickfield count are incidental.

china-1919:p0116_1.rationale: List of chemical works and locations.

china-1919:p0116_2.rationale: List of confectionery manufacturers at Harbin; no confectionery tag in vocabulary (food-processing is a broad fit but a confectionery list is narrow).
review_questions: Should a confectionery or food-processing tag be applied to confectionery manufacturer lists?

china-1919:p0116_3.rationale: List of cotton spinning and weaving works with locations.

china-1919:p0117_1.rationale: Continuation list of cotton spinning and weaving mills with locations.

china-1919:p0117_2.rationale: List of vodka distilleries with owners and locations in Manchuria.

china-1919:p0118_1.rationale: List of breweries with nationality and location.

china-1919:p0118_2.rationale: List of aerated water manufacturers, followed by dock and engineering works; mixed textual lists with no single fitting tag (shipbuilding and machinery are substantial but the heading is aerated water).
review_questions: Does the table combine aerated water makers with dockyards and engineering works under one heading, needing a beverage or soft-drinks tag or splitting?

china-1919:p0119_1.rationale: Directory of two egg factories with locations; no quantities. Egg processing fits food processing; eggs-and-poultry is about primary production, so it was not used.

china-1919:p0119_2.rationale: List of cities supplied with electric light and current; purely textual place names with no quantities.

china-1919:p0120_1.rationale: List of flour mills and their locations; flour milling falls under food processing. No quantities.

china-1919:p0132_1.rationale: Counts of silk filatures and spinning machines by town, 1915-1917; this is silk reeling capacity.

china-1919:p0133_1.rationale: Years when Western nations first had direct trade dealings with China. This is a short chronology of events; the years are dates, not statistical quantities.

china-1919:p0142_1.rationale: Staff numbers of the Chinese Maritime Customs indoor service by grade, foreign and Chinese; this is administrative personnel.

china-1919:p0142_2.rationale: Outdoor Customs staff counts by grade and nationality; administrative personnel.

china-1919:p0142_3.rationale: Customs coast staff counts (commanders, officers, engineers, and others) by foreign and Chinese; administrative personnel.

china-1919:p0143_1.rationale: Staff numbers of the Customs Marine Department (coast, harbours, lights, marine), foreign and Chinese; administrative personnel.

china-1919:p0143_2.rationale: Staff numbers of the Customs Works Department; administrative personnel.

china-1919:p0144_1.rationale: Native customs revenue collected at each port in Haikuan taels for 1914-1917, with totals; this is revenue by port.

china-1919:p0144_2.rationale: Lists customs stations/treaty ports with province, opening date, treaty basis and estimated Chinese population, organised around the treaty-port system. The mixed table includes population figures, so it is statistical.

china-1919:p0146_1.rationale: Textual list of places opened to trade by agreement with foreign powers, including leased and ceded territories. No quantities; dates are only agreement references. No exact tag for open places beyond the treaty ports.
review_questions: Propose a tag for places opened to foreign trade outside treaty ports (self-opened ports)?

china-1919:p0147_1.rationale: Lists Yangtze ports of call with service type and treaty/regulation authority; textual with no quantities.
review_questions: Propose a tag for ports of call or river stages under treaty authority?

china-1919:p0147_2.rationale: Lists West River ports of call with service type and treaty authority; textual with no quantities.
review_questions: Propose a tag for ports of call or river stages under treaty authority?

china-1919:p0147_3.rationale: Open ports ranked by total customs revenue collected in 1917 in Haikwan taels.

china-1919:p0148_1.rationale: Descriptive list of Customs Marine Department lighting districts and their coastal/river limits; textual geographic limits, no quantities.

china-1919:p0149_1.rationale: Counts of lights, light-vessels, light-boats, buoys and beacons by Customs district.

china-1919:p0150_1.rationale: Chronological list of China's treaties and agreements with dates and subject matter; textual treaty list.

china-1919:p0152_1.rationale: List of treaty with Austria-Hungary with date and subject, plus a note on multilateral agreements; textual.

china-1919:p0152_2.rationale: Lists two China-Belgium treaties by date and subject; textual treaty list.

china-1919:p0153_1.rationale: Textual list of treaties and conventions with Brazil, Congo Free State, Denmark and France, including indemnity, lease and boundary subjects.

china-1919:p0154_1.rationale: Single China-Italy treaty entry; textual treaty list.

china-1919:p0154_2.rationale: Single China-Korea treaty entry; textual treaty list.

china-1919:p0154_3.rationale: List of China-Japan treaties and agreements, 1885-1909, covering peace, cession, commerce and Manchurian railways; textual treaty index.

china-1919:p0155_1.rationale: Textual treaty list for Japan (continued), Mexico, Netherlands, Peru, Portugal and Russia by date and subject.

china-1919:p0156_1.rationale: Chronological textual list of China-Russia treaties and agreements with subject matter.

china-1919:p0157_1.rationale: Two China-Spain treaties listed by date and subject; textual.

china-1919:p0157_2.rationale: Two China treaties with Sweden and Norway listed by date and subject; textual.

china-1919:p0157_3.rationale: Textual list of China-United States treaties and conventions 1844-1908 with subjects.

china-1919:p0157_4.rationale: A one-row list of an agreement between Great Britain and Belgium (exchange of notes on trade-mark protection in China), giving date, place and subject. The content is textual and concerns an interstate agreement.

china-1919:p0157_5.rationale: Textual list of agreements between Great Britain and other powers concerning China. It covers trade marks, concessions at Hankow, the occupation of Weihaiwei, alliance terms and the opium traffic. Interstate agreements are the main subject, and foreign privileges in China (concessions, Yunnan and Szechuan privileges, Weihaiwei occupation) are a substantial secondary theme.

china-1919:p0159_1.rationale: Textual list of agreements among foreign powers about China. It covers railway interests, the integrity of China, Tibet, Manchuria and the annexation of Korea. Dates and subjects are the substantive content. The agreements concern foreign spheres of interest in a nominally sovereign China.

china-1919:p0160_1.rationale: Annual average value of the Haikuan tael in sterling, dollars, francs, marks, rupees and yen, 1899-1917. These are currency exchange equivalents.

china-1919:p0161_1.rationale: Annual customs revenue by import, export, coast trade and tonnage duties, 1906-1917. It is a customs-revenue series.

china-1919:p0161_2.rationale: Customs revenue components, including tonnage dues, transit dues and opium likin, with totals, 1906-1917. Opium likin is a specific likin component.

china-1919:p0161_3.rationale: Duties on native produce exported to foreign countries and to Chinese ports. They are customs revenue arising from exports.

china-1919:p0161_4.rationale: Customs revenue split between foreign trade and home trade, 1906-1917, with totals.

china-1919:p0162_1.rationale: Total customs revenue by port, 1907-1911, in Haikwan taels, with a grand total. The figures are revenue, not trade values.

china-1919:p0163_1.rationale: Continuation of the port-by-port total revenue series for 1912-1917, with a total that matches the annual revenue totals. The context calls the values trade, but the title and totals indicate customs revenue. The port names are missing from the transcription.
review_questions: The context describes the figures as trade values, but the title and totals match customs revenue; confirm the measure.

china-1919:p0164_1.rationale: Annual gross imports, exports of Chinese produce, re-exports and totals in Haikwan taels, 1902-1917.

china-1919:p0164_2.rationale: Sterling restatement of gross imports, exports of Chinese and foreign produce, and totals for 1911-1917.

review_questions: Does the later restarted numbering belong to the export series rather than imports?

china-1924-5:p0534_1.rationale: Continued export statistics by commodity (metals, ores, cement, wool, silk), with quantities and values for 1920-22.

china-1924-5:p0535_1.rationale: Continued export statistics by commodity covering raw materials and manufactured goods, with quantities and values for 1920-22.

china-1924-5:p0538_1.rationale: Export statistics for machinery, vehicles and instruments. The figures are unreadable in the transcription, but the structure establishes a quantitative export table.

china-1924-5:p0539_1.rationale: Export statistics for manufactured goods, arms and gold and silver, with a total, for 1920-22.

china-1924-5:p0540_1.rationale: Value of direct imports from and exports to each country or colony for 1918-22, with totals.

china-1924-5:p0542_1.rationale: Direct trade values with each country 1918-1922, split into imports from and exports to each country; the rows are trade flows by partner.

china-1924-5:p0545_1.rationale: Continuation of the direct trade by country table (Australia, South Africa); ends with total imports, less re-exports to foreign countries, net imports and exports.

china-1924-5:p0546_1.rationale: Whole trade of each port (Aigun to Tientsin) in 1921 and 1922, split into net foreign imports, net Chinese imports and exports with port totals. It is port-level trade, not treaty-port institutional content.

china-1924-5:p0547_1.rationale: Continued whole trade by port (Lungkow to Yochow): net foreign imports, net Chinese imports, exports and totals.

china-1924-5:p0548_1.rationale: Continued whole trade by port (Hankow to Ningpo): net foreign imports, net Chinese imports and exports with port totals.

china-1924-5:p0549_1.rationale: Continued whole trade by port (Wenchow to Lappa, incl. Kowloon): imports, Chinese imports, exports and totals.

china-1924-5:p0550_1.rationale: Continued whole trade by port (Kongmoon to Szemao): net foreign imports, net Chinese imports, exports and totals for 1921 and 1922.

china-1924-5:p0551_1.rationale: Tengyueh plus grand totals of foreign imports, Chinese imports and exports, with value of exports abroad and home trade.

china-1924-5:p0552_1.rationale: Value of re-exports of foreign goods to each foreign country in 1921 and 1922, with direct and Hongkong totals.

china-1924-5:p0553_1.rationale: Carrying trade by flag in 1922: vessel entries, tonnage, foreign imports carried, import duties and tonnage dues. Combines shipping tonnage by nationality with trade values and duties.
review_questions: Is a vocabulary term needed for carrying trade by flag or tonnage dues?

china-1924-5:p0554_1.rationale: Outward clearances and tonnage by flag, with export values, re-exports and export duties; shipping is the principal subject, with export trade and duties as substantial parts.

china-1924-5:p0555_1.rationale: Coast carrying trade between open ports by flag: clearances, tonnage, Chinese export and re-export values, export duties and tonnage dues.
review_questions: Is there a tag for coastal trade between ports? Domestic-trade is the closest fit.

china-1924-5:p0556_1.rationale: Coast trade inwards by flag: entries, tonnage, import values and coast trade duties between open ports.

china-1924-5:p0557_1.rationale: Shares of each flag in entries, clearances, tonnage and trade values of foreign and coast trade.

china-1924-5:p0558_1.rationale: Percentage share of each nationality in carrying trade by tonnage, trade value and customs duties and dues.

china-1924-5:p0559_1.rationale: Import, export and coast duties and tonnage dues by flag; customs revenue is the main measure.

china-1924-5:p0560_1.rationale: Transit trade values inwards and outwards by port, 1922.

china-1924-5:p0560_2.rationale: Continuation of transit trade values by port from Harbin to Shanghai.

china-1924-5:p0561_1.rationale: Shanghai gross and net trade values 1919-1922: imports, re-exports of foreign and Chinese goods, and local-origin exports.

china-1924-5:p0563_1.rationale: Export values by commodity direct to foreign countries, with 1913 comparisons and recalculation at 1913 prices; a multi-commodity export table.

china-1924-5:p0564_1.rationale: Exports by commodity direct to foreign countries, with declared values and values recalculated at 1913 prices. The table is a multi-commodity export list, so no single commodity tag fits.

china-1924-5:p0571_1.rationale: Annual silk production by type (white, yellow, steam filature, wild, waste), 1910-1922, with some cocoon columns. The silk tag covers the material and its output; cocoons are only one column, so sericulture is not added.

china-1924-5:p0581_1.rationale: Half-yearly quantity of cotton consumed in China by cotton type, in bales. It measures consumption by mills.

china-1924-5:p0581_2.rationale: Cotton mill stocks by cotton type at two half-year dates.

china-1924-5:p0582_1.rationale: Shanghai cotton mills, spindles and looms by Chinese, Japanese and British ownership. The ownership split is a breakdown of the cotton industry.

china-1924-5:p0583_1.rationale: Proposed new cotton mills in Manchuria listed by company, with capital, spindles, looms and nationality.

china-1924-5:p0587_1.rationale: Customs movement of vegetable tallow, quantity and value, for 1921 and 1922. No vocabulary tag covers tallow or wax, and the table does not clearly separate imports from exports.
review_questions: Propose a tag for vegetable tallow and wax products.

china-1924-5:p0588_1.rationale: Estimated walnut quantities by province. Walnuts fit no specific tag; horticulture is an approximate fit but not clearly supported.
review_questions: Propose a tag for nuts or tree crops such as walnuts.

china-1924-5:p0589_1.rationale: Exports of brown and white sugar in piculs and taels for 1921 and 1922.

china-1924-5:p0592_1.rationale: Vermicelli exports from the Chefoo trade in piculs and taels for 1921 and 1922.

china-1924-5:p0598_1.rationale: Quantities of opium seized from named steamers in June 1923 on river traffic; seizures are enforcement of opium control.

china-1924-5:p0609_1.rationale: Maritime Customs confiscations of opium, morphia, cocaine/heroin and poppy seed in 1923 are seizure results; opium and morphine are substantial components.

china-1924-5:p0610_1.rationale: Estimated opium production by country in the East, with China the largest.

china-1924-5:p0641_1.rationale: Chinese and Turki monetary denominations and equivalences used in Sinkiang, a description of the monetary system.
review_questions: Could measurement-and-units also apply to these denomination equivalences, or is currency sufficient?

china-1924-5:p0665_1.rationale: List of Anglican bishops by diocese with consecration dates; the content is textual, and dates are incidental.

china-1924-5:p0666_1.rationale: Foreign Protestant mission personnel in 1921 by district and category (ordained, physicians, nurses, single women, totals).

china-1924-5:p0667_1.rationale: Chinese Protestant mission workforce in 1921 by district and category (evangelists, teachers, medical staff), with ratios to foreign workers.

china-1924-5:p0668_1.rationale: Protestant congregations, evangelistic centres, communicants by sex, literacy and Christian community totals by district in 1921.

china-1924-5:p0669_1.rationale: Protestant mission lower primary, higher primary and middle schools and pupils by district, boys and girls.

china-1924-5:p0670_1.rationale: Protestant mission hospitals, dispensaries, beds, inpatients, nurse schools and beds per foreign physician by district in 1921.

china-1924-5:p0671_1.rationale: Ratios of Protestant missionary occupation by district: communicants, missionaries, Chinese workers, hospital beds, physicians and mission students. Missions fits best as the main subject.

china-1924-5:p0672_1.rationale: Roster of Catholic bishops and vicars apostolic with sees, names, titular sees, birth years and consecration dates. The content is textual; years are only identifiers.

china-1924-5:p0673_1.rationale: Continuation roster of Catholic bishops and vicars apostolic grouped by congregation. The content is textual, with dates as incidental identifiers.

china-1924-5:p0674_1.rationale: Statistics for Roman Catholic vicariates: bishops, European and Chinese priests, Christians, annual increase and catechumens.

china-1924-5:p0674_2.rationale: Regional summary totals of Catholic bishops, priests, Christians and annual increase.

china-1924-5:p0674_3.rationale: Ratios of Christians per priest (foreign and Chinese) for Catholic missions. The figures are quantitative, although some are unreadable.

china-1924-5:p0695_1.rationale: Monthly budget of a middle-class Peking family in 1922 against 1912, itemised, to show the rise in living costs.

china-1924-5:p0695_2.rationale: Peking prices of cloth, foodstuffs and coal across four years, presented to illustrate the labourer's cost of living.

china-1924-5:p0700_1.rationale: Percentage breakdown of causes of strikes in China, September to December 1922.

china-1924-5:p0704_1.rationale: List of Western nations with the year each first traded directly with China. It is a short chronological list, and the years are only dates. No existing tag fits it well.
review_questions: Should a tag for early foreign trade contacts be added?

china-1924-5:p0719_1.rationale: Gross imports, exports of Chinese and foreign produce, and totals by year for China's foreign trade 1913-1922.

china-1924-5:p0719_2.rationale: Net imports (gross less re-exports), exports and totals by year; the note on re-exported foreign goods is substantive.

china-1924-5:p0720_1.rationale: Textual list of the five lighting districts of the coast and their geographic limits, for the Marine Department's lighting of aids to navigation.

china-1924-5:p0721_1.rationale: Native customs revenue by port for 1920-1922, including the famine relief surtax; it is a customs revenue table.

china-1924-5:p0722_1.rationale: Counts of lights, light-vessels, light-boats, buoys and beacons by customs district for 1923.

china-1924-5:p0723_1.rationale: Numbered customs districts with their coastal and river limits; textual list of jurisdictions.
review_questions: Should a customs-jurisdiction tag be proposed? Administrative-divisions is the nearest fit.

china-1924-5:p0723_2.rationale: Treaty ports by province, opening date, treaty power and estimated Chinese population in 1920; organised around the treaty-port system, with population figures making it mixed.

china-1924-5:p0724_1.rationale: Places opened to trade in Mongolia and Manchuria with the agreement country and year; textual list organised around treaty-opened places.

china-1924-5:p0725_1.rationale: Continuation of treaty ports, marts and places opened, with the opening authority and date; textual list.

china-1924-5:p0725_2.rationale: Ports of call on Yangtze and West River with permitted traffic and the agreements that opened them; textual list on river navigation under treaty agreements.
review_questions: Is a tag for treaty river stages needed? None exists in the vocabulary.

china-1924-5:p0727_1.rationale: Textual list of foreign concessions and settlements at Chinese treaty ports; no quantities.

china-1924-5:p0727_2.rationale: Dated list of China's treaties (mainly with Great Britain) with textual subject summaries, plus the Washington Conference and Austria-Hungary entries. Treaty content includes cessions and indemnity but the principal subject is the treaty list.

china-1924-5:p0729_1.rationale: List of China's treaties with Belgium: dates and subjects in text.

china-1924-5:p0729_2.rationale: China-Bolivia treaty entry with date and subject, text only.

china-1924-5:p0729_4.rationale: China-Congo Free State treaty entry, text only.

china-1924-5:p0729_6.rationale: Treaty lists with France, Germany, Italy, Korea and Japan; dates and textual subject matter.

china-1924-5:p0731_1.rationale: Continuation of treaty lists (Japan, Mexico, Netherlands, Persia, Peru, Portugal, Russia) with dates and textual subjects.

china-1924-5:p0732_1.rationale: Treaty lists with Russia, Spain, Sweden and Norway, Switzerland and the United States; textual subject descriptions.

china-1924-5:p0733_1.rationale: A list of treaties between other powers concerning China, with dates and subject matter. The content is textual and treaty-based; entries cover concessions, privileges and spheres of interest.

china-1924-5:p0734_1.rationale: A textual list of treaties and agreements concerning China, grouped by party, with dates and subjects.

china-1924-5:p0736_1.rationale: Quantities of copper coins minted by denomination, showing the scale of subsidiary coinage issue.

china-1924-5:p0736_2.rationale: Number of 10-cash copper pieces per dollar at treaty ports, showing the depreciation of copper coinage. The measure is a copper-cash/dollar exchange rate.
review_questions: Does copper cash against dollar quotation warrant foreign-exchange, or is it domestic currency valuation only?

china-1924-5:p0737_1.rationale: Copper ingot imports into Hankow by source in pounds, cited as evidence of copper coinage depreciation. Imports of a commodity with copper as the material.

china-1924-5:p0737_2.rationale: Monthly highest, lowest and average dollar exchange rates in Peking in 1923, expressed in coppers.

china-1924-5:p0737_3.rationale: Paper money in circulation by province, with amounts issued, market value and discounted value.

china-1924-5:p0738_1.rationale: Depreciated bank note amounts by province, with redemption rates and values.

china-1924-5:p0739_1.rationale: Principal taels current in China by place, with silver content in grains and comparative values. It documents monetary standards and their equivalence.

china-1924-5:p0741_1.rationale: Annual Haikwan tael equivalents in several foreign currencies from 1910 to 1923, i.e. exchange values.

china-1924-5:p0742_1.rationale: Equivalences between Kuping, Haikwan, Shanghai and local taels at treaty ports are monetary-unit conversions within China's currency system.
review_questions: Tael equivalence between local taels is not exchange between currencies; a tag for monetary units or tael equivalence could be proposed.

china-1924-5:p0753_1.rationale: Assay weight and fineness of silver dollars minted at a Chinese mint concern the metallic content of coinage.

china-1924-5:p0754_1.rationale: Weight and fineness assays of Mint B dollars for 1916 and 1920 describe coin metallic content.

china-1924-5:p0754_2.rationale: Weight and fineness assays of Mint C dollars in 1920 describe coin metallic content.

china-1924-5:p0754_3.rationale: Weight and fineness assays of Mint D dollars across 1915-1920 describe coin metallic content.

china-1924-5:p0767_1.rationale: Treasure (gold, silver, copper coin) imported into China in 1922 by country of origin, valued in Haikwan taels.
review_questions: Gold and silver bullion imports are mixed with coin; no specific tag for treasure/bullion flows exists.

china-1924-5:p0768_1.rationale: Treasure (gold, silver, copper coin) exported from China in 1922 by destination, in Haikwan taels.
review_questions: No specific tag for treasure/bullion flows.

china-1924-5:p0769_1.rationale: Annual imports, exports and net balances of gold, silver and merchandise 1913-1922.

china-1924-5:p0770_1.rationale: Numbers of gold, silver and copper coins by type moved across borders in 1922, by country; coin circulation is the main subject.
review_questions: A tag for coin movements or treasure flows could be proposed.

china-1924-5:p0771_1.rationale: Yearly lowest and highest London quotations of the Shanghai tael with ranges and year-on-year differences, 1890-1907.

china-1924-5:p0772_1.rationale: Yearly lowest and highest London telegraphic transfer selling rates for the Chinese dollar, 1908-1923, with ranges and differences; this is exchange-rate data.

china-1924-5:p0775_1.rationale: Monthly average, lowest and highest Shanghai exchange rates for 1923 (4 m/s credits, TT, bar silver) with dates of extremes.

china-1924-5:p0776_1.rationale: Conversion table of traditional Chinese weight units (li, fen, ch'ien, liang, chin, tan).

china-1924-5:p0776_2.rationale: Equivalents of liang, catty and picul in avoirdupois and metric units, fixed for foreign trade; a weights conversion table.

china-1924-5:p0777_1.rationale: Number of catties per picul of rice, wheat, beans and maize by province, showing variation in measurement standards in native trade. The focus is on units, not crop output.

china-1924-5:p0777_2.rationale: Conversion equivalents between cwt, ton, kilogram and catty.

china-1924-5:p0777_3.rationale: Traditional Chinese length units and their relations.

china-1924-5:p0777_4.rationale: Standard lengths of the ch'ih in inches across different trades; a measurement standards table.

china-1924-5:p0778_1.rationale: Traditional Chinese area units and their equivalences.

china-1924-5:p0778_2.rationale: Traditional Chinese capacity units (ko, sheng, tow, shih) and their relations.

china-1924-5:p0780_1.rationale: Comparative Republican budget revenue by source (land tax, customs, salt, likin) with ordinary and extraordinary receipts, loans, and expenditure by ministry; a general public budget.

china-1924-5:p0781_1.rationale: Extraordinary expenditure by ministry across five budget years, with totals; a public budget account.

china-1924-5:p0781_2.rationale: Ordinary, extraordinary and total government expenditure by budget year.

china-1924-5:p0781_3.rationale: Itemised components of income directly received by the central government (stamp duty, tobacco and wine taxes, mining duty) in 1919, part of the budget revenue.

china-1924-5:p0786_1.rationale: Five principal government revenue sources (customs, salt gabelle, wine and tobacco taxes, stamp duty) with amounts collectable.

china-1924-5:p0788_1.rationale: Central Government revenue by source, comparing five-year average and latest figures with estimates of future collections.

china-1924-5:p0789_1.rationale: Central government administrative expenses by department, ordinary and contingent, from the 8th Year budget.

china-1924-5:p0789_2.rationale: Annual amortization amounts required for secured loan obligations of the Ministry of Finance, 1924-1933; a debt repayment schedule.

china-1924-5:p0791_1.rationale: Monthly expenditure by military division, brigade and police unit in the central government budget; army expenses are the principal subject, with police also included.

china-1924-5:p0792_1.rationale: Continuation of monthly Ministry of War expenses by unit, school, arsenal and depot, with total expenses.

china-1924-5:p0793_1.rationale: Monthly expenses of Chihli army divisions, brigades, gendarmes and hospital; military units with cost amounts.

china-1924-5:p0793_2.rationale: Monthly expenses of miscellaneous troops (new troops, cavalry, patrol battalions, bodyguard).

china-1924-5:p0793_3.rationale: Monthly expenses of the offices of Governors-General and Vice-Governor-General; administrative office costs.

china-1924-5:p0793_4.rationale: Monthly naval expenses: Ministry of Navy officers and river patrol commands and cruisers.

china-1924-5:p0794_1.rationale: Detailed monthly central government expenses by office (presidency, parliament, cabinet, ministries) with section totals.

china-1924-5:p0795_1.rationale: Continuation of monthly expenses of the Ministry of the Interior bureaus with a total.

china-1924-5:p0795_2.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Ministry of Finance and its subsidiary bureaus.

china-1924-5:p0795_3.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Ministry of War and subsidiary organs such as General Staff, colleges and aviation bureau.

china-1924-5:p0795_4.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Ministry of Navy and naval attaches abroad.

china-1924-5:p0795_5.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Ministry of Justice, courts, procuratorates, prisons and extraterritoriality commission.

china-1924-5:p0796_1.rationale: Continuation of the monthly central government expense list: the special-area prisons item and the Ministry of Justice total. This is public expenditure by item.

china-1924-5:p0796_2.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Ministry of Education, covering its colleges, schools, student funds abroad and subsidies, with a total. It is both a central budget item and education funding.

china-1924-5:p0796_3.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce and its stations and bureaus. Primarily a central government expenditure list.

china-1924-5:p0796_4.rationale: Ministry of Communications monthly expense, consisting solely of the Vladivostok railway supervision association. It is a budget line.

china-1924-5:p0796_5.rationale: Monthly expenses of the Bureau for Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs, including its school and allowances to princes. It is a central government expenditure list.

china-1924-5:p0797_1.rationale: Remaining central government monthly expense items (Mongolian and Tibetan bureau, imperial pensions) and the grand total of fifteen sections. It is budget expenditure.
review_questions: Is a tag for imperial pensions needed? Existing tags only partly fit, and imperial-household is not clearly about pension finance.

china-1924-5:p0797_2.rationale: Surplus of maritime and native customs revenue for 1921, in taels, available to meet the government deficit.

china-1924-5:p0797_3.rationale: Salt surplus released, revenue detained by the provinces and special items paid from the surplus, October 1921 to September 1922. It concerns the fiscal salt revenue.

china-1924-5:p0798_1.rationale: Collections of the Peking octroi and their earmarked monthly funds (notes redemption, schools, judiciary reform, students in Japan). The octroi is a local levy and the table shows how its revenue is allocated.
review_questions: Is a tag for octroi or local levies needed?

china-1924-5:p0798_2.rationale: Amounts of mining, stamp, wine and tobacco, and income taxes and government property profits actually received by the central government.

china-1924-5:p0799_1.rationale: Summary of domestic and foreign government loans, secured and unsecured, with totals; a public indebtedness table.

china-1924-5:p0804_1.rationale: Lists secured domestic government loans with amounts issued and outstanding; domestic debt only.

china-1924-5:p0806_1.rationale: Secured foreign debts with amounts borrowed and outstanding, interest rates and periods, including Boxer indemnity obligations by country.

china-1924-5:p0806_2.rationale: Totals of secured foreign debts converted to dollars at stated exchange rates.

china-1924-5:p0808_1.rationale: Deferred debts owed to Germany and Austria with amounts, interest, extinction dates and security.

china-1924-5:p0808_2.rationale: Summary of German debts by place and currency with an approximate dollar total.

china-1924-5:p0809_1.rationale: Domestic loans not definitely secured: consolidation bonds with issued and outstanding amounts.

china-1924-5:p0810_1.rationale: Unsecured foreign debts with original and outstanding amounts, interest rates and contract dates.

china-1924-5:p0811_1.rationale: Continuation of unsecured foreign debts with amounts, interest rates and dates.

china-1924-5:p0812_1.rationale: Totals of unsecured foreign debts by currency converted to dollars, with explanatory notes on items.

china-1924-5:p0817_1.rationale: Lists short-term loans from Chinese banks brought before the debt redemption commission, with outstanding amounts, bond face values and balances to be redeemed; this is government debt with bank creditors.

china-1924-5:p0818_1.rationale: Continuation of the short-term loan statement with banks and companies as lenders, giving original, outstanding and redeemable amounts under the 10th Year bonds.

china-1924-5:p0822_1.rationale: Treasury notes issued to organisations in lieu of payment of expenditure, with original and outstanding amounts, interest rates and issue dates; this is government debt.

china-1924-5:p0827_1.rationale: Statement of short-term internal debts with banks and companies, giving original and outstanding amounts and monthly or annual interest rates.

china-1924-5:p0828_1.rationale: Continuation of short-term internal debts with outstanding amounts, interest rates and contract dates.

china-1924-5:p0829_1.rationale: Totals of outstanding short-term internal debts converted to dollars at stated rates, with notes on repayment terms.

china-1924-5:p0831_1.rationale: Summary of capital and interest totals across classes of domestic, foreign and short-term loans not definitely secured.

china-1924-5:p0832_1.rationale: General statement of liabilities of the Ministry of Communications, with railway, telegraph and postal obligations, principal paid and outstanding; debt is primary and railway obligations are a substantial component.

china-1924-5:p0833_1.rationale: Scale of stamp duty by face value of Class (b) documents, a tax rate schedule.

china-1924-5:p0834_1.rationale: Maritime Customs collections by port in 1922 with increases over the previous year.

china-1924-5:p0834_2.rationale: Maritime Customs collections by port for 1923 with year-on-year variation; this is customs revenue.

china-1924-5:p0838_1.rationale: Cash statement of receipts and payments of the National Consolidated Loan Service: coupons cashed, bonds redeemed, sinking fund and balances.

china-1924-5:p0838_2.rationale: Lists liabilities for unpaid interest coupons and drawn but unredeemed bonds covered by the year-end loan service cash balance.

china-1924-5:p0839_1.rationale: Schedule of 1923 loan redemptions and interest by date, loan and drawing, with total obligation.

china-1924-5:p0839_2.rationale: Computes total loan service liability for 1923, receipts and arrears on government loans.

china-1924-5:p0840_1.rationale: Lists loan drawings due for redemption that make up the obligation in arrears.

china-1924-5:p0841_1.rationale: Statement of national and consolidated loans: issued, drawn and outstanding principal, interest rates, dates and 1924 payments.

china-1924-5:p0841_2.rationale: Lists consolidated loan drawings in arrears on 1 January 1924 with due dates and amounts.

china-1924-5:p0842_1.rationale: Allotment of the Boxer indemnity among the Powers by percentage, taels and foreign currency under the 1901 Protocol.

china-1924-5:p0848_1.rationale: Salt Administration revenue account listing loan and indemnity charges secured on salt revenue for 1921-1923. The debt-service component is the main focus.
review_questions: Would a tag for salt revenue securing loans (salt-revenue-securities) be useful? The existing salt-tax tag may not fit because the table shows loan charges rather than tax receipts.

china-1924-5:p0848_2.rationale: Salt Revenue Account balances, net collections and interest credited by the Group Banks, 1921-23. This is a fiscal account of salt revenue.

china-1924-5:p0849_1.rationale: Salt Revenue Account with the Group Banks: releases to the central government, retained and appropriated revenue, and sums refunded by the Maritime Customs. The subject is salt revenue allocation.
review_questions: Is a tag for revenue sharing between central and provincial authorities needed?

china-1924-5:p0850_1.rationale: District inspectorates' salt releases, revenue receivable and received, expenses and transfers to the group banks. Salt quantities are given, but the table is mainly about fiscal revenue.

china-1924-5:p0851_1.rationale: Salt released and revenue receivable by district inspectorate, 1919-21. The fiscal framing is the salt gabelle.

china-1924-5:p0852_1.rationale: Salt revenue received and outstanding by district inspectorate, 1919-21.

china-1924-5:p0853_1.rationale: Expenses incurred by each salt district inspectorate, 1919-21, as part of salt revenue administration.

china-1924-5:p0853_2.rationale: Transfers of salt revenue to the group banks, 1919-21. The district labels are blank in the transcription, but the totals match the transfers column of the preceding salt table.

china-1924-5:p0855_1.rationale: Graduated income tax rate scale for Class II incomes, with an exemption threshold.

china-1924-5:p0858_1.rationale: Average likin receipts by province, used as the basis for distributing increased duties under the abolition plan.

china-1924-5:p0858_2.rationale: Annual receipts from likin and similar inland transit taxes by category, to be apportioned in the abolition scheme.

china-1924-5:p0865_1.rationale: Lists six Chinese Government loans by interest rate and name. The content is a textual list of foreign-issued loans without amounts, so foreign-loans fits and the table is non-statistical.

china-1924-5:p0869_1.rationale: Gives amounts of each Chinese loan, the German issue, the amount outstanding and the amount validated. These are foreign loan balances.

china-1924-5:p0881_1.rationale: Foreign claims by country and category arising from the Lincheng outrage, presented in dollars. This is an interstate claims matter; no vocabulary tag fits claims for compensation, which are distinct from treaty indemnities.
review_questions: Propose a tag for diplomatic claims or compensation for incidents.

china-1924-5:p0895_1.rationale: Lists the payment method each signatory power selected for Boxer indemnity payments. The content is textual.

china-1925-6:p0188_2.rationale: Estimated oil shale reserve at Fushun by depth, a reserve estimate for a petroleum-related resource.

china-1925-6:p0189_2.rationale: Manufactured asbestos output in catties by the Tientsin Co., 1918-1923. No existing tag covers asbestos or building-material manufacture of this kind.

china-1925-6:p0189_3.rationale: List of mining laws with dates, promulgating authority and article counts; the content is a legal list, and the article counts are only incidental identifiers.

china-1925-6:p0190_1.rationale: Index of mining regulations with dates, issuing authorities and page references; textual list of legislation.

china-1925-6:p0191_1.rationale: List of mining regulations for special areas (Heilungkiang gold mines, Kirin small mines) with date, promulgating authority and article counts; content is textual, regulatory mining legislation.

china-1925-6:p0196_1.rationale: Output of the Fangtze group of coal mines by lump, bulk and mixed coal and in total, 1918-1921.

china-1925-6:p0196_2.rationale: Annual Tzuchuan coal field output by coal type, 1916-1921.

china-1925-6:p0197_1.rationale: Percentages of cephalic (head-shape) types in the living population of China proper, a physical-anthropology measurement. No existing tag covers physical anthropology or racial type.

china-1925-6:p0200_1.rationale: Textual classification of Shan and Tibeto-Burman aboriginal peoples into groups and subgroups, with no quantities. Ethnological classification only.

china-1925-6:p0203_1.rationale: List of Manchu dynasty rulers with reign years, supporting a historical summary. The reign dates are incidental to a textual roster. The ruler succession does not match the narrower imperial-household definition (court, royal family and household institutions).

china-1925-6:p0267_1.rationale: Silk filature in Hupeh with its number of spindles, i.e. silk reeling capacity.

china-1925-6:p0267_2.rationale: Silk filature at Chinkiang, Kiangsu, with its number of spindles, i.e. silk reeling capacity.

china-1925-6:p0267_4.rationale: Lists Soochow silk filatures with spindle numbers.

china-1925-6:p0267_5.rationale: Lists Nanking silk filatures with spindles; context mentions workforce incidentally.

china-1925-6:p0268_1.rationale: Kwangtung silk filature factories with spindle counts.

china-1925-6:p0299_1.rationale: Shansi higher, middle and primary schools: numbers, students and revenue, plus overseas scholarship expenditure, across 1916-1922.

china-1925-6:p0307_1.rationale: List of universities and colleges with location, founding year and control; content is essentially textual.

china-1925-6:p0308_1.rationale: Mission school presiding officers with teacher counts, enrolment, average age and library volumes. Mission affiliation is only implied by officers and abbreviations, so no mission-schools tag.

china-1925-6:p0309_1.rationale: National amateur field and track records with holders and years.

china-1925-6:p0310_1.rationale: Swimming records with times and holders.

china-1925-6:p0310_2.rationale: National middle school athletic records by event, holder, school and year.

china-1925-6:p0312_1.rationale: Schools, students by sex and expenses by school type in 1923; school and pupil totals are the main subject, with an expense column.

china-1925-6:p0313_1.rationale: Students by grade (elementary, secondary, college) for each province.

china-1925-6:p0314_1.rationale: Christian lower primary, higher primary and middle schools and students by province. Mission-school affiliation is plausible, but the table does not show mission operation explicitly.
review_questions: Should Christian schools here carry mission-schools, or christianity?

china-1925-6:p0315_1.rationale: Various Christian institutions (normal, Bible, medical, blind, deaf, orphanage, kindergarten) with student numbers; the mixed school types are summarised under schools and pupils.

china-1925-6:p0322_1.rationale: Vessels arriving at Tientsin Bund in selected years, with maximum draught, illustrating river and harbour improvement; this is port arrival traffic.

china-1925-6:p0335_1.rationale: Maritime Customs revenue by duty type, 1914-1923.

china-1925-6:p0335_2.rationale: Customs revenue apportioned between foreign and home trade by year.

china-1925-6:p0335_3.rationale: Export duties on Chinese produce, shipped to foreign countries or to Chinese ports, as the basis for revenue apportionment.

china-1925-6:p0336_1.rationale: Total maritime customs revenue of each port, 1919-1923.

china-1925-6:p0337_1.rationale: A degraded column of revenue figures from the customs revenue section with famine relief surtax notes; labels are unreadable, but the intended quantities are statistical and the section is customs revenue. Tags are withheld because the labels cannot be read and the content cannot be confirmed.
review_questions: Can the labels be recovered to confirm customs-revenue and famine-relief-surtax content?

china-1925-6:p0339_1.rationale: Customs revenue collected at each port for 1919-1923, with totals and famine surtax footnotes. The subject is revenue by port.

china-1925-6:p0340_1.rationale: Direct foreign trade imports and exports by port, 1922 and 1923. The ports are the treaty-port units of the customs returns.

china-1925-6:p0341_1.rationale: Direct foreign trade by port with imports, exports and totals, plus re-export totals and a net total.
review_questions: Table title and the two column sets are unlabelled, so the years are not identified.

china-1925-6:p0342_1.rationale: Gross imports by commodity for 1921-1923, covering living animals, foods and beverages and raw materials, with quantities and values. No single commodity dominates.
review_questions: Propose an aggregate tag for commodity-classified trade statistics.

china-1925-6:p0345_1.rationale: Imports by quantity and value for plants, fodder, timber, dye-woods and common metals, 1921-1923. The items are diverse.
review_questions: Propose an aggregate tag for commodity-classified trade statistics.

china-1925-6:p0346_1.rationale: Imports classified by goods across manufactured products, textiles, machinery and bullion, with a grand total. Covers many commodities, including a repeated start of the exports/second part.

Propose an aggregate tag for commodity-classified trade statistics.

china-1925-6:p0353_1.rationale: Exports of food articles (cereals, flour, vegetables, tea, sugar, oils, salt, beverages), with quantity and value for 1921-1923.
review_questions: Propose an aggregate tag for commodity-classified trade statistics.

china-1925-6:p0354_1.rationale: Continuation of exports of raw and prepared materials (skins, bones, hair, oil-cake, seeds, tobacco, timber), 1921-1923.
review_questions: Propose an aggregate tag for commodity-classified trade statistics.

china-1925-6:p0355_1.rationale: Exports of metals, minerals, textiles and other articles by quantity and value, 1921-1923. Many commodities appear, so no single commodity tag is used.
review_questions: Propose an aggregate tag for commodity-classified trade statistics.

china-1925-6:p0356_1.rationale: Continuation of exports covering textile fibres and manufactured products, with quantities and values for 1921-1923.
review_questions: Propose an aggregate tag for commodity-classified trade statistics.

china-1925-6:p0358_1.rationale: Continuation of customs export statistics listing many goods (building materials, metals, machinery, gold and silver) by quantity and value, with total exports.

china-1925-6:p0361_1.rationale: Direct imports from and exports to each country and region, 1919-1923, in Haikwan taels.

china-1925-6:p0366_1.rationale: Direct trade with Australia and South Africa plus total imports, re-exports to foreign countries, net imports and exports for 1919-23.

china-1925-6:p0367_1.rationale: Whole trade of each northern port: net foreign imports, net Chinese imports, exports and port totals 1922-23.

china-1925-6:p0368_1.rationale: Trade of each port (Lungkow, Chefoo, Kiaochao, Yangtze river ports): net foreign and Chinese imports, exports and totals for 1922-23.

china-1925-6:p0369_1.rationale: Trade values by port (Hankow, Shanghai, Ningpo etc.): net foreign imports, net Chinese imports, exports and port totals 1922-23.

china-1925-6:p0370_1.rationale: Southern and western ports' trade values with grand totals, and exports abroad versus home trade, 1922-23.

china-1925-6:p0373_1.rationale: Value of foreign goods re-exported from China to each country and Hongkong, 1922-23.

china-1925-6:p0374_1.rationale: Foreign import trade by carrying flag: ship entries, tonnage, import values, import duties and tonnage dues.

china-1925-6:p0375_1.rationale: Outward clearances and tonnage by flag, with export values, re-exports and export duties for China's foreign carrying trade in 1923.

china-1925-6:p0377_2.rationale: Coast-trade inward entries and tonnage by flag, a purely shipping measure.

china-1925-6:p0379_1.rationale: Import, export and coast-trade duties and tonnage dues by flag, a customs revenue breakdown by carrier nationality.

china-1925-6:p0380_1.rationale: Percentage shares of each flag in trips, tonnage, trade values and duties and dues for the carrying trade.

china-1925-6:p0381_1.rationale: Value of transit trade inwards and outwards at southern and coastal treaty ports in 1923.

china-1925-6:p0381_2.rationale: Value of transit trade inwards and outwards at northern and Yangtze ports, ending with Shanghai, in 1923.

china-1925-6:p0382_1.rationale: Gross and net values of Shanghai's foreign and Chinese-produce imports, re-exports and exports, 1920-1923. Two readings are unreadable but the structure shows the intended quantities.

china-1925-6:p0387_1.rationale: Numbered list of four Manchurian and Mongolian railway lines covered by the 1918 loan. It is textual, with no quantities. Railway lines are the subject.

china-1925-6:p0394_1.rationale: Railway lines under contract, with the state of each scheme and approximate mileage. The mileages are quantitative, so the table is mixed text and statistics. The subject is railway development.
review_questions: A tag for railway concessions or contracts, or for foreign railway loans, may be needed; none fits the vocabulary.

china-1925-6:p0400_1.rationale: National railway operating statistics for 1923 and 1922: kilometres operated, revenue, expenses, passengers, tons carried and train kilometres.

china-1925-6:p0401_1.rationale: Distribution of railway investment assets by construction and financial accounts for each line, ending in the total cost carried to the balance sheet. The substance is capital cost accounts of railways.

china-1925-6:p0402_1.rationale: Continuation of the 1923 railway investment asset distribution for the remaining lines, with the all-lines total for Chinese Government Railways.

china-1925-6:p0403_1.rationale: Cost of road and equipment, kilometres owned and cost per kilometre by line for 1923, plus a series for all Government Railways, 1916-1923.

china-1925-6:p0404_1.rationale: Condensed operating and income accounts by railway for 1923: revenues, expenses, income debits and credits, and year-end balances.

review_questions: Consider a vocabulary term for rolling stock or locomotives.

china-1925-6:p0417_1.rationale: Two rows of railway locomotives by number, type, wheel arrangement, weight and maker.
review_questions: Consider a vocabulary term for rolling stock or locomotives.

china-1925-6:p0421_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of the Hupeh-Hunan railway section by number, type, wheels, weight and maker.
review_questions: Consider a vocabulary term for rolling stock or locomotives.

review_questions: Consider a vocabulary term for rolling stock or locomotives.

review_questions: Consider a vocabulary term for rolling stock or locomotives.

china-1925-6:p0427_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of the Lunghai Railway by type, wheel arrangement, weight and maker; railway rolling stock.

china-1925-6:p0430_1.rationale: Locomotive stock by number, type, wheel arrangement, weight and maker for a railway; railway rolling stock.

china-1925-6:p0431_1.rationale: Passenger, sleeping, dining and baggage coaching vehicles counted by class and type; railway rolling stock.

china-1925-6:p0432_2.rationale: Lengths of principal tunnels on the Dairen-Mukden line; railway infrastructure.

china-1925-6:p0433_1.rationale: Locomotives of a foreign-owned railway by tank type, wheels, weight, maker and gauge; railway rolling stock.

china-1925-6:p0434_1.rationale: Locomotives of the Chinese Eastern Railway by number, type, wheels, weight and maker; railway rolling stock.

china-1925-6:p0441_1.rationale: Roads constructed or under construction by province, with route endpoints, condition, mileage and builder; road infrastructure.

china-1925-6:p0455_1.rationale: Number of post offices taking part in international C.O.D. parcel exchange, grouped by partner countries. Statistical.

china-1926-7:p0371_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of the Chinese Eastern Railway by number, type, wheel layout, weight and maker.

china-1926-7:p0381_1.rationale: Roads in Shansi and Honan with endpoints, condition, length in li and builder; mixed table with length quantities.

china-1926-7:p0389_1.rationale: Yearly packages, weight and letters carried for Minchu agencies by the post office.

china-1926-7:p0391_2.rationale: Foreign employees of the Chinese Posts counted by nationality; the institution is the postal service, and the nationality breakdown is secondary.

china-1926-7:p0393_1.rationale: Counts of post offices participating in the international C.O.D. parcel service, grouped by the countries with which they exchange parcels.

china-1926-7:p0395_1.rationale: Growth of the Chinese Post Office 1906-1924: offices, articles and parcels posted, courier and steamer lines.

china-1926-7:p0395_2.rationale: Cash-on-delivery parcel numbers, values and weights handled by the post, 1919-1924. This is postal service volume.

china-1926-7:p0396_1.rationale: Mail volumes (letters, postcards, printed matter) by country, comparing China's postal traffic with other nations. The population column is only a denominator.

china-1926-7:p0396_2.rationale: Classes of money order offices with codes and issue or cashing limits. The content is a descriptive classification rather than statistical quantities; the limits are rule parameters.

china-1926-7:p0396_3.rationale: Value of postal money orders issued and cashed by year, 1904-1924.

china-1926-7:p0399_1.rationale: Foreign postal agencies in China closed in 1922, by nationality and closure date. This reflects foreign privileges in the postal sector.
review_questions: Propose a tag for foreign post offices in China.

china-1926-7:p0401_1.rationale: District counts of post offices, agencies and offices with special functions (money order, savings, parcel insurance) at the end of 1924.

china-1926-7:p0402_1.rationale: Letters and other articles posted for local delivery by district, 1924 with 1923 totals.

china-1926-7:p0405_1.rationale: Packages, weight and letters posted by Min-Chü (private letter hongs) by district, 1921-1924.

china-1926-7:p0406_1.rationale: Ordinary, insured and C.O.D. parcels posted by district in 1924: number, value and weight.

china-1926-7:p0407_1.rationale: Number and declared value of insured mail items posted by postal district, 1923 and 1924; this is postal service activity.

china-1926-7:p0408_1.rationale: Telegrams handled by the post office for the telegraph office, by district; the subject is telegram traffic.

china-1926-7:p0409_1.rationale: Money orders issued by district, with numbers and values for two years, through the postal channel.

china-1926-7:p0409_2.rationale: Money orders cashed by district, with numbers and values, through the postal channel.

china-1926-7:p0410_1.rationale: Lengths in li of postal courier, steamer and railway mail lines by district.

china-1926-7:p0411_1.rationale: Postal Savings Bank deposits, withdrawals and balances due to depositors, in the Big Dollar and Small Coin accounts.

china-1926-7:p0411_2.rationale: Postal Savings Bank investments by security (loans, debentures, bonds, deposits, property) at the end of 1924.

china-1926-7:p0412_1.rationale: Small Coin Account investments of the postal savings system, including loans, fixed deposits, property and mortgages.

china-1926-7:p0412_2.rationale: Floating balance of the postal savings accounts held at Peking headquarters and in the districts.

china-1926-7:p0413_1.rationale: Operating statistics of the Chinese Government telegraph system: lines, cables, instruments, offices and traffic.

china-1926-7:p0413_2.rationale: Lengths and construction dates of principal telegraph lines; quantitative telegraph network data.

china-1926-7:p0413_3.rationale: Per-word domestic telegram rates by destination and language; telegraph tariffs.
review_questions: Vocabulary lacks a communications tariff/charges tag; telegraph used for the service.

china-1926-7:p0414_1.rationale: Telegraph offices (wire and wireless), line routes and wire lengths by province for 1925.

china-1926-7:p0417_1.rationale: Inventory of wireless stations with ranges, power, wavelengths, ownership and controlling authority; mixed quantitative and descriptive content. Radiotelegraph is within radio/telegraph. Many are foreign-controlled, but the table is primarily a technical station list.
review_questions: Does foreign military control of stations justify an informal-imperialism or foreign-garrisons label?

china-1926-7:p0419_1.rationale: Continuation of wireless station list with range, antenna power, system, wavelength and remarks.

china-1926-7:p0419_2.rationale: Wireless stations by city, ownership, controlling authority, call signal, range and power; includes foreign-controlled stations in leased territories but main subject is station inventory.

china-1926-7:p0420_1.rationale: Wireless stations by location, control, range, power, system and wavelength.

china-1926-7:p0421_1.rationale: Count of radio stations by controlling nation and planned stations to be erected by a foreign company, with power figures.

china-1926-7:p0423_1.rationale: Numbered list of ports and rivers whose conservancy works are described; purely textual list.

china-1926-7:p0427_1.rationale: Number of vessels crossing the Bar to Tientsin and their maximum draught, 1900-1925; port access measures.

china-1926-7:p0444_1.rationale: Middle school counts of schools, students, teachers, per-student cost and ratios for 1912, 1916 and 1922-23, with percentage changes.

china-1926-7:p0458_1.rationale: Numbered list of national universities with locations; no quantities.

china-1926-7:p0458_2.rationale: List of private institutions approved by the Ministry of Education, with locations; textual.

china-1926-7:p0458_3.rationale: List of private institutions on probation, with locations; textual.

china-1926-7:p0459_1.rationale: List of universities not yet inspected by the Ministry of Education, with locations; textual.

china-1926-7:p0461_1.rationale: Attendance at Catholic Church schools by grade, 1923, with a total.

china-1926-7:p0464_1.rationale: China Foundation grants to educational institutions: annual, special and first-year amounts.

china-1926-7:p0465_1.rationale: China Foundation appropriations to institutions and educational or research projects, with sub-totals and grand total.

china-1926-7:p0466_1.rationale: Library holdings of prominent college libraries, split into Chinese and Western books, with totals.

china-1926-7:p0473_1.rationale: Mission college students classified by the type of middle school they came from, with the share from Christian schools.

china-1926-7:p0477_1.rationale: Comparative Republican budgets showing revenue by source and expenditure by ministry for several budget years; land tax and customs are the leading revenue items.

china-1926-7:p0478_1.rationale: Itemised income directly received by the central government in 1919 (stamp duty, tobacco and wine, mining duty), together with figures for inadequately secured obligations.

china-1926-7:p0479_1.rationale: Outstanding principal of secured loans by category: domestic bonds, treasury notes, foreign loans and Boxer indemnities.

china-1926-7:p0480_1.rationale: Amounts of unsecured public loans by category, including domestic bonds, treasury notes, bank advances and foreign loans.

china-1926-7:p0481_1.rationale: Maritime Customs revenue by duty type for 1922-24 in taels and dollars.

china-1926-7:p0483_1.rationale: Inland native customs receipts, collecting expenses and net receipts by customs house.

china-1926-7:p0488_1.rationale: Wine and tobacco taxes remitted to the central government by district, 1921-1923.
