china-1926-7:p0490_1.rationale: Postal department gross receipts, administrative expenditure, extension spending and balance, an operating account of the postal service.

china-1926-7:p0493_1.rationale: Likin revenue by province: amount collected, cost of collection and net receipts.

china-1926-7:p0498_1.rationale: Itemised inadequately secured foreign loans with creditor, amounts, interest rates, security and outstanding balances at 31 December 1925.

china-1926-7:p0503_1.rationale: Danish creditor's Kungshien Arsenal loan with terms, security and outstanding amounts.

china-1926-7:p0504_1.rationale: Austrian loan with interest terms, security and outstanding balances converted to Chinese dollars.

china-1926-7:p0506_1.rationale: Secured debts of the Ministry of Communications summarised by currency with Chinese dollar equivalents; foreign obligations dominate.

china-1926-7:p0506_2.rationale: Inadequately secured Ministry of Communications debts by currency, with combined totals in Chinese dollars.

china-1926-7:p0507_1.rationale: Summary of secured Ministry of Communications obligations (railway, telegraph, telephone loans, materials) with unpaid principal and arrears; largely foreign-currency loans.

china-1926-7:p0516_1.rationale: Telephone materials obligations owed to suppliers (China-Japan Industrial Development Co., China Electric Co.), with unpaid principal and arrears; these are supplier credits rather than clearly loans.

china-1926-7:p0517_1.rationale: Fixed conversion rates of foreign currencies and taels into Chinese dollars used for calculating the Ministry's debts.

china-1926-7:p0517_2.rationale: Lists loans (railway advances, telegraph loan) included in the Ministry of Finance consolidation plan with amounts in yen and sterling.

china-1926-7:p0518_1.rationale: Outstanding principal and interest of six categories of inadequately secured domestic government loans, bonds, treasury notes and bank advances.

china-1926-7:p0519_1.rationale: Schedule of secured loan service payments due in 1926, with amounts in several foreign currencies (sterling, yen, francs, florins), so mainly foreign loans and debt service.

china-1926-7:p0520_1.rationale: Continued schedule of principal and interest instalments on secured loans due in 1926, mostly in foreign currencies.

china-1926-7:p0524_1.rationale: Continuation of the 1926 secured loan payment schedule with principal and interest amounts in sterling and dollars.

china-1926-7:p0525_1.rationale: Continuation of the 1926 secured loan payment schedule across many loans, currencies and due dates.

china-1926-7:p0532_1.rationale: Graded stamp duty scale by face value of documents, a tax rate schedule.

china-1926-7:p0539_2.rationale: Payments of loan redemption and interest in 1925 by loan, drawing and coupon, including repayment of bank advances.

china-1926-7:p0539_3.rationale: Closing cash balance of the National Loan Service at end of 1925, part of the loan service accounts.

china-1926-7:p0571_2.rationale: Percentage loss on converting copper-cent income into dollars shows copper-coin depreciation; the Shanghai Tramways appear only as the source of the data.

china-1926-7:p0572_2.rationale: Sources of silver bars reaching Shanghai over four years (imports from the U.S.A., London and Eastern ports) form a bullion import table.

china-1926-7:p0572_3.rationale: Estimated uses of imported silver bars for coinage versus sycee and the arts bear on the monetary use of silver.

china-1926-7:p0590_1.rationale: Numbers of gold, silver and copper coins exported, by destination and coin type.

china-1926-7:p0621_1.rationale: Continued bank list with establishment, head office, branches and capital figures.

china-1926-7:p0623_1.rationale: Final bank list page with head offices, branches and authorized and paid-up capital.

china-1928:p0168_1.rationale: Port-by-port trade values for Lungkow to Yochow: imports, Chinese trade, exports and totals.

china-1928:p0169_1.rationale: Port-by-port trade values Hankow to Ningpo: imports, Chinese trade, exports and totals.

china-1928:p0170_1.rationale: Port trade values Wenchow to Lappa, split into imports, Chinese trade and exports.

china-1928:p0171_1.rationale: Minor ports' trade values with grand totals and the division of exports into abroad and home trade.

china-1928:p0173_1.rationale: Re-exports of foreign goods by destination country, 1924 and 1925.

china-1928:p0174_1.rationale: Vessel entries and tonnage by flag, with foreign import values, import duties and tonnage dues.

china-1928:p0175_1.rationale: Clearances and tonnage by flag, with export and re-export values and export duties.

china-1928:p0176_1.rationale: Coast carrying trade between open ports by flag: clearances, tonnage, export and re-export values, export duties and tonnage dues. Shipping is the main subject; re-exports and customs duties are substantial columns.

china-1928:p0177_1.rationale: Inward coast trade by flag: entries, tonnage, Chinese and foreign import values and import duties.

china-1928:p0178_1.rationale: Foreign and coastwise carrying trade by flag, combining tonnage with import, export and coast trade values.

china-1928:p0179_1.rationale: Duties and tonnage dues paid by each flag on foreign and coast trade; customs revenue by nationality of carrying vessels.

china-1928:p0180_1.rationale: Percentage shares of each flag in trips, tonnage, trade and dues revenue. Shipping is the clear subject; other aspects are mixed percentages.

china-1928:p0181_1.rationale: Value of transit trade inwards and outwards at each port, 1925. Transit trade is the explicit subject. The treaty-ports tag is weakly supported, so it is dropped.

china-1928:p0182_1.rationale: Shanghai gross and net trade values for 1922-1925: foreign imports, re-exports of foreign and Chinese goods, and exports of local produce.

china-1928:p0184_1.rationale: Monthly prevalence signs (+, ++, +++) for plague, cholera, smallpox and other communicable diseases by province in 1926. The marks are a graded intensity scale rather than counts, but the table is statistical in intent.

china-1928:p0185_1.rationale: Continuation of monthly communicable-disease prevalence for further provinces, Hongkong and Kansu in 1926.

china-1928:p0187_1.rationale: Monthly communicable-disease prevalence for Shansi, Manchuria, Kweichow and Kwangtung in 1926, with graded plus-sign marks.

china-1928:p0188_1.rationale: Monthly presence marks for thirteen communicable diseases by province in 1926; the rows and columns are about disease occurrence. The table is a mixed symbol-based statistical table.

china-1928:p0191_1.rationale: Case counts of plague, smallpox, cholera and other major infectious diseases in Amoy for 1924-26.

china-1928:p0208_1.rationale: Number and size of vessels that the Antung-area ports can accommodate, which is a port capacity measure.

china-1928:p0211_1.rationale: Pilotage charges per foot of draught at Newchwang for steam and sail vessels; these are harbour service charges.

china-1928:p0213_1.rationale: Vessels crossing the Bar to reach Tientsin Bund, with maximum draught, in selected years. The context presents it as showing improvement of the Hai Ho, a conservancy result.

china-1928:p0218_1.rationale: Shipping dues by ship tonnage and cargo handling at Weihaiwei, Tsingtao and Haichow harbours; these are port charges.

china-1928:p0225_1.rationale: Dimensions of dry docks in Shanghai harbour; these are port facilities. The vocabulary has no dry-dock or port-facilities tag, though ports fits broadly.
review_questions: Is a tag for dock and port facilities needed?

china-1928:p0225_2.rationale: Pilotage tariff per foot and per ton for routes around Shanghai, Woosung, Gutzlaff and Tungsha.

china-1928:p0226_1.rationale: Wharfage dues per unit of goods (silk, tea, treasure) at Shanghai harbour; these are port charges on traded goods, not commodity data.
review_questions: Is a port-charges tag needed?

china-1928:p0231_1.rationale: Pilotage charges per registered ton for sailing vessels on the Canton and Whampoa route.

china-1928:p0231_2.rationale: Pilotage tariff for steamers at Canton/Whampoa, with charges scaled by draught; a transport charge schedule.
review_questions: Pilotage as a port service has no dedicated tag; freight-and-transport-costs is the closest fit.

china-1928:p0232_1.rationale: Additional pilotage fees for vessels above Whampoa, berth shifting and pilot retention charges; transport service charges.
review_questions: Consider a dedicated pilotage or port-charges tag.

china-1928:p0236_1.rationale: Yearly initial output of one-cent copper coins, 1904-1908, illustrating overproduction of copper currency.

china-1928:p0237_1.rationale: Number of copper cents per dollar at Shanghai, 1912-1925, showing depreciation of the copper currency against the dollar. It is a domestic exchange rate between coin types, so the currency tag suits it.

china-1928:p0237_2.rationale: Percentage loss on converting copper-cent income into dollars, used to illustrate copper currency depreciation. The tramway company is the example, not the subject.

china-1928:p0238_1.rationale: Total imports, exports and net imports of bar silver and sycee in Haikwan taels over 1892-1925; a commodity trade table concerning silver.

china-1928:p0238_2.rationale: Silver bars imported to Shanghai in 1926 by origin (U.S.A., London, Eastern ports); silver bullion movement.

china-1928:p0238_3.rationale: Uses of imported silver bars in 1926: coinage versus conversion into sycee and the arts.

china-1928:p0239_1.rationale: Weight and fineness of the principal taels current in China; monetary unit standards.

china-1928:p0239_2.rationale: Schedule converting 100,000 troy ounces of bar silver at various finenesses into Shanghai tael proceeds; a unit conversion table.

china-1928:p0241_1.rationale: Gross weight, fineness and fine-silver content of dollar coins circulating in China; this concerns coin composition within the monetary system.

china-1928:p0243_1.rationale: Customs values of gold imported and exported 1890-1925, with the net excess of exports; this is gold trade, not reserves.

china-1928:p0246_1.rationale: Annual highest and lowest official sterling telegraphic transfer quotations, 1890-1926.

china-1928:p0249_1.rationale: Monthly highest and lowest Shanghai T.T. exchange rates on London, New York, Paris and Kobe, with yearly averages.

china-1928:p0250_1.rationale: Monthly highest and lowest Shanghai T.T. exchange rates on Hongkong, India, Batavia and the Straits Settlements, 1924-1926.

china-1928:p0251_1.rationale: Monthly highest, lowest and average exchange rates for bar silver, sterling and US dollars, 1926-27.

china-1928:p0252_1.rationale: Annual average exchange rates of the Haikwan tael against several foreign currencies, 1914-1926.

china-1928:p0252_2.rationale: Annual average T.T. rate on London against Shanghai taels, 1909-1926.

china-1928:p0253_1.rationale: Annual imports, exports and net balances of gold, silver and merchandise in Haikwan taels, 1916-1925; this is trade in bullion and goods.

china-1928:p0254_1.rationale: Annual silver movement from customs statistics, split into coin and bars/sycee, with net exports; this is bullion trade in silver.

china-1928:p0254_2.rationale: Annual silver imports into China by bars and coin, with net imports, compiled from Maritime Customs. This is trade in silver as a bullion commodity and in coin. The vocabulary has no tag for general bullion or specialie movements; silver/imports tags would be weak since the table covers both directions of flow.
review_questions: Should a tag for specie or bullion movements be added? The existing silver tag is for mining and commodity data, and imports alone does not cover the table's two-way flows.

china-1928:p0255_1.rationale: Annual gold exports from China by bars/dust and coin with net exports, from Customs statistics. Under the rules, gold exports are trade with exports and gold.

china-1928:p0255_2.rationale: Annual gold imports into China by bars/dust and coin with net imports, from Customs statistics. Under the rules, gold imports are trade with imports and gold.

china-1928:p0262_1.rationale: Monthly turnover of gold bars at the Shanghai Gold Stock Exchange, 1924-1926. The subject is the trading volume of an exchange.

china-1928:p0262_2.rationale: Yearly yen value of gold bar turnover at the Shanghai Gold Stock Exchange, derived from the registered bar turnover. The subject is exchange trading activity.

china-1928:p0264_1.rationale: Liabilities side of the half-year balance sheet of the Shanghai Gold Stock Exchange: capital, reserves, broker margins, creditors and profit. These are the accounts of a business enterprise.

china-1928:p0264_2.rationale: Assets side of the Shanghai Gold Stock Exchange balance sheet, covering securities, property, loans and cash. These are company accounts.

china-1928:p0264_3.rationale: Profit and loss account of the Shanghai Gold Stock Exchange for the half-year, showing expenses, brokerage and interest receipts. These are company operating accounts.

china-1928:p0264_4.rationale: Allocation of the Shanghai Gold Stock Exchange's half-year net profit among taxes, reserve, staff bonus and dividend. These are company profit-appropriation accounts.

china-1928:p0267_1.rationale: List of foreign banks operating in China in June 1927 with year of establishment, head office, branches and authorized and paid-up capital. It is a bank inventory, and the foreign-owned capital holdings fit foreign investment. It also records joint Sino-foreign enterprises.

china-1928:p0268_1.rationale: Foreign banks in China with founding year, head office, branches and authorized and paid-up capital; this is a bank inventory.

china-1928:p0269_1.rationale: Japanese banks in China as of June 1927, with branches and authorized and paid-up capital in yen.

china-1928:p0270_1.rationale: Continuation giving branch locations and authorized and paid-up capital in yen for Japanese banks in China.

china-1928:p0270_2.rationale: List of Japanese banks with head office and establishment year only; the content is textual and there are no substantive quantities.

china-1928:p0271_1.rationale: Four Japanese banks with branches and authorized and paid-up capital in yen.

china-1928:p0272_1.rationale: List of Chinese banks, June 1927, with head offices, branches and capital figures.

china-1928:p0276_1.rationale: Chinese banks with head office, year established, branches and authorized and paid-up capital.

china-1928:p0277_1.rationale: Continued list of Chinese banks with branches and capital figures.

china-1928:p0279_1.rationale: Authorized and paid-up capital and branches of Chinese banks, continued from the previous page.

china-1928:p0279_2.rationale: Chinese banks listed by name, establishment year, head office and branches; the content is textual with no capital quantities.

china-1928:p0280_1.rationale: List of Chinese banks with founding year, head office, branches and authorized and paid-up capital; banking is the subject.

china-1928:p0281_1.rationale: Continued list of banks with head offices, branches and capital; banking is the subject.

china-1928:p0282_1.rationale: Multi-page continued bank list with establishment year, branches and capital figures; banking is the subject.

china-1928:p0288_1.rationale: Legal units of length, area, capacity and weight with metric and English equivalents; a measurement standards table.

china-1928:p0288_2.rationale: Native weight units and their relations, with a gramme equivalent.

china-1928:p0288_3.rationale: Weights fixed for foreign trade with avoirdupois and metric equivalents; a unit conversion table.

china-1928:p0288_4.rationale: Native length units from fen to li with metric values.

china-1928:p0288_5.rationale: Length of the ch'ih for Customs trade in inches and metres; a unit equivalence.

china-1928:p0289_1.rationale: Varying ch'ih standard lengths by trade; a metrology table.

china-1928:p0289_2.rationale: Ch'ih values in inches for Shanghai and nearby cities by commodity; a metrology table.

china-1928:p0289_3.rationale: Table gives equivalences among Chinese units of area (ssu, hao, li, fên, mow, ch'ing), a measurement conversion table.

china-1928:p0289_4.rationale: Table gives square measure equivalents (square ch'ih, pu, mow, ch'ing), a unit conversion table.

china-1928:p0296_1.rationale: Lists distances in miles of South Manchuria Railway main and branch lines with a total.

china-1928:p0304_1.rationale: Inventory of Chinese railways with opening dates and mileage open and under construction, including government, provincial and concessioned lines. Mixed numbers and text, so statistical.

china-1928:p0308_1.rationale: List of railway lines under contract with scheme status, concessions and loan agreements, and approximate mileage. Principal subject is railways; concession and loan content is secondary. Mileage figures make it a mixed table.
review_questions: Foreign railway concessions and loan contracts are substantial here; consider whether a tag for railway concessions or loans is needed.

china-1928:p0314_1.rationale: Compares Chinese government railway operating statistics (km operated, revenue, passengers, tons, employees) for 1924 and 1923 with percentage changes.

china-1928:p0315_1.rationale: Distribution of railway construction and financial accounts (investment assets) by line for 1924, with cost carried to balance sheet. Railway capital accounts.
review_questions: Printed totals do not add up in several columns; kept as read.

china-1928:p0316_1.rationale: Continuation-style table of 1924 railway investment assets by construction and financial accounts for further lines and Chinese Government Railways total.

china-1928:p0317_1.rationale: Cost of road and equipment and cost per kilometre by railway line for 1924, with Chinese Government Railways yearly series 1915-1924.

china-1928:p0318_1.rationale: Condensed operating and income accounts for 1924 by railway line: revenues, expenses, income debits and credits, balances.
review_questions: Some cells are unreadable ([?]); structure still establishes a statistical table.

china-1928:p0319_1.rationale: Operating revenues by item (passenger, goods, rents) for Peking-Hankow and Peking-Mukden railways; railway accounts.

china-1928:p0319_2.rationale: Operating revenues by item for Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo and Peking-Suiyuan railways; railway accounts.

china-1928:p0319_3.rationale: Operating revenues by item for Tientsin-Pukow and Shanghai-Nanking railways; railway accounts.

china-1928:p0319_4.rationale: Operating revenues by item for Taokow-Chinghua and Cheng-Tai railways; railway accounts.

china-1928:p0320_1.rationale: Continued 1924 operating revenue analysis for Kaifeng-Honan, Lung-Hai, Kirin-Changchun and Canton-Kowloon railways.

china-1928:p0320_2.rationale: Continued 1924 operating revenue analysis for Hupeh-Hunan, Ssu-Tao, Kiao-Tsi and total Chinese Government Railways.

china-1928:p0321_1.rationale: Operating expenses by department (general, traffic, running, maintenance) for eight railway lines in 1924; railway accounts.

china-1928:p0322_1.rationale: Continued 1924 operating expenses analysis by department for several railways.

china-1928:p0323_1.rationale: Profit and loss account (credits, debits, surplus or deficit) for six railway lines; railway accounts.

china-1928:p0323_2.rationale: 1924 profit and loss statement for further Chinese railways and total government railways; row labels unreadable but structure shows railway accounts.
review_questions: Row labels are unreadable, so the specific credit and debit items are unidentified.

china-1928:p0324_1.rationale: Railway operating expenses by category for four named lines, with amounts and percentages. The values are unreadable but the structure shows they are quantitative. The subject is railway operating accounts.
review_questions: No tag exists for railway operating costs or accounts, so only railways is used.

china-1928:p0326_1.rationale: Capital and invested surplus of the Peking-Mukden Railway. It shows government capital, British and Japanese loans, and accumulated surplus revenue as financial accounts of a railway.
review_questions: Foreign-loans could apply to the British and Japanese loan lines, but the table is mainly a capital account, so it is omitted.

china-1928:p0327_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of the Peking-Mukden line by type, wheel arrangement, weight and maker, with a total of 225. This is railway rolling stock.

china-1928:p0329_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of the Tientsin-Pukow Railway by number, tender or tank type, wheel arrangement, weight and builder. This is railway rolling stock.

china-1928:p0329_2.rationale: Number of coaching and service vehicles by class on the Tientsin-Pukow Railway. This is railway rolling stock.

china-1928:p0330_1.rationale: Goods wagons by type, with a total of 2,086. The footnote mentions civil-war disruption but this is incidental. This is railway rolling stock.

china-1928:p0330_2.rationale: Lengths in feet of the principal railway bridges, listed by river locality. This is railway infrastructure.
review_questions: The roads-and-bridges tag is for road infrastructure, so it is not used for these railway bridges.

china-1928:p0331_1.rationale: Locomotive stock by number, type, wheel arrangement, weight and maker for the Shanghai-Nanking railway, as shown by the maker shop abbreviations. This is railway rolling stock.

china-1928:p0332_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of the Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railway by number, type, wheel arrangement, weight and maker, with a total of 42. This is railway rolling stock.

china-1928:p0334_1.rationale: Locomotive stock by class, number, wheel arrangement, average weight, maker and type, with a total of 138. This is railway rolling stock.

china-1928:p0336_1.rationale: Railway locomotive stock by number, type, wheel arrangement and weight; railway equipment statistics.

china-1928:p0337_1.rationale: Unpaid principal and interest on a railway mortgage bond loan by year; debt service amounts. Railway context is secondary to the liabilities shown.
review_questions: Is the Pekin Syndicate loan a foreign loan (foreign-loans)? Not explicit in the table, so not tagged.

china-1928:p0337_2.rationale: Outstanding sterling loan principal, interest and rolling stock liabilities converted to dollars with wages added; railway liabilities.
review_questions: Is the debt a government liability or a railway's own? Not stated, so public-debt is the closest tag.

china-1928:p0338_1.rationale: Locomotive roster of a railway by number, type, wheels, weight and maker.

china-1928:p0342_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of a railway line by number, wheel arrangement, weight and maker. Footnotes give revenue and expenditure totals.

china-1928:p0345_1.rationale: Locomotives held by a railway by number, type, weight and maker.

china-1928:p0346_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of a railway with weights and makers, total 108.

china-1928:p0346_2.rationale: Principal railway bridges with lengths and span arrangements; bridge infrastructure data.
review_questions: Roads-and-bridges excludes railway bridges tabulated only as railway assets; is railways a better tag here?

china-1928:p0348_1.rationale: Locomotive stock of the Lunghai railway by type, wheels, weight and maker.

china-1928:p0348_2.rationale: Principal bridges on the eastern and western sections of the Lung Hai Railway by kilometre location and spans; treated as railway assets.

china-1928:p0349_1.rationale: Lists mortgage bond issues of the Szechwan-Hankow Railway by year, currency, amount and rate/term, held by Belgian and Dutch syndicates; this is railway debt owed to foreign lenders.

china-1928:p0352_1.rationale: Locomotive stock by number, type, wheel arrangement, weight and maker for a railway (South Manchuria Railway makers named); rolling stock inventory.
review_questions: Vocabulary lacks a rolling-stock tag; railways used.

china-1928:p0353_1.rationale: Inventory of passenger and service coaching vehicles by class and bogie type on a railway.

china-1928:p0353_2.rationale: Counts of goods wagons by type on a railway.

china-1928:p0353_3.rationale: Number and span lengths of principal railway bridges between named stations; railway infrastructure.
review_questions: Railway bridges excluded from roads-and-bridges; no railway-infrastructure tag exists.

china-1928:p0354_1.rationale: Lengths of principal tunnels on the Antung-Mukden railway section; railway infrastructure.

china-1928:p0355_1.rationale: Locomotive stock by number, tank type, weight and maker, including a 2 ft gauge line.

china-1928:p0355_2.rationale: Motor coaches on a standard-gauge railway: number, power, weight and maker.

china-1928:p0356_1.rationale: Locomotives of the Chinese Eastern Railway by number, type, wheel arrangement, weight and maker.

china-1928:p0363_1.rationale: List of roads reported constructed by province, endpoints, condition, length in miles and constructing agency; road infrastructure.

china-1928:p0367_1.rationale: Lists road routes by province with condition, length and construction authority (provincial, private, local); this is road infrastructure.

china-1928:p0373_1.rationale: Yearly packages, weight and letters carried by Minchu private agencies; postal mail traffic.

china-1928:p0375_1.rationale: Chinese Post Office staff by grade in 1908 and 1926; postal administration personnel counts.
review_questions: Vocabulary lacks a tag for postal staffing; postal-services is the nearest fit.

china-1928:p0375_2.rationale: Number of foreign employees of the Chinese Post Office by nationality; postal staff composition.

china-1928:p0377_1.rationale: Counts of post offices participating in the international C.O.D. parcel service, grouped by partner countries; parcel mail service.

china-1928:p0379_1.rationale: Growth of the Chinese postal service 1906-1925: offices, articles and parcels posted, courier and boat lines.

china-1928:p0379_2.rationale: Number, value and weight of cash-on-delivery parcels handled by the post office yearly 1919-1925.

china-1928:p0380_1.rationale: Comparative postal mail volumes by type and per-head averages for China and other countries.

china-1928:p0380_2.rationale: Classes of money order offices with issue and cashing limits; postal money order system.

china-1928:p0380_3.rationale: Value of postal money orders issued and cashed yearly 1904-1925.

china-1928:p0381_1.rationale: Annual income, working expenses, surplus and capital expenditure of the Chinese Post Office. Postal operation with financial accounts; no tag for postal accounts specifically, so postal-services is used.
review_questions: Should a tag be added for the operating accounts of public enterprises?

china-1928:p0383_1.rationale: Counts foreign postal agencies in China by nationality and the date each ceased operation after the Washington Conference. This concerns foreign privileges in a nominally sovereign state and mail services.
review_questions: Is a tag needed for foreign postal agencies or privileges beyond foreign-concessions?

china-1928:p0385_1.rationale: Mail matter posted by class (letters, postcards, newspapers etc.) in each postal district in 1925. The Total column is unreadable but the quantitative structure is clear.

china-1928:p0385_2.rationale: Postal statistics for 1925 by district: registered, express and insured articles, local delivery, and insured values in dollars, francs and yen.

china-1928:p0387_1.rationale: Number of post offices, agencies and box offices by district at the end of 1925, including offices with special functions such as money orders and savings banks.

china-1928:p0388_1.rationale: Letters and other articles posted for local delivery in each district in 1925.

china-1928:p0389_1.rationale: Packages, weight and letters contained in mail posted by Min-Chü (a postal category) by district for 1922-1925.

china-1928:p0390_1.rationale: Ordinary, insured and C.O.D. parcels posted in 1925 by district: number, value and weight.

china-1928:p0391_1.rationale: Number and insured value of insured mail posted by district in 1924 and 1925, in dollars, francs and yen.

china-1928:p0392_1.rationale: Telegrams handled by the Post Office on behalf of the Telegraph Office in 1925, by district, split by whether accepted directly or received from the Telegraph Office.

china-1928:p0393_1.rationale: Domestic money orders cashed by district, with numbers and values for 1924 and 1925; the postal money-order channel is explicit.

china-1928:p0393_2.rationale: Domestic money orders issued by district, with numbers and values for 1924 and 1925.

china-1928:p0394_1.rationale: Mail service routes in li by district, split into courier, steamer and boat, and railway lines.

china-1928:p0395_1.rationale: Post Office Savings Bank deposits, opening balances, transfers and interest credited by district for 1925.

china-1928:p0396_1.rationale: Post Office Savings Bank credits, withdrawals and transfers by district for 1925.

china-1928:p0397_1.rationale: Post Office Savings Bank balances due to depositors and account numbers opened, closed and open by district at the end of 1925.

china-1928:p0398_1.rationale: Receipts account of the Post Office Savings Bank for 1925: interest, exchange gains and fees, and a drawing from the Postal Advance Account. It is a financial account of a postal savings institution.
review_questions: Is a tag for institutional financial accounts or operating accounts needed? Existing tags (savings-and-loans, banking) fit only partly.

china-1928:p0398_2.rationale: Profit and loss account of the Post Office Savings Bank for 1925: interest paid, exchange losses, charges and working expenses.
review_questions: Is a tag for institutional financial accounts or operating accounts needed? Existing tags (savings-and-loans, banking) fit only partly.

china-1928:p0399_1.rationale: Continued Post Office Savings Bank profit and loss account for small coin currency, with an interest and exchange account.
review_questions: Is a tag for institutional financial accounts or operating accounts needed? Existing tags (savings-and-loans, banking) fit only partly.

china-1928:p0400_1.rationale: Balance sheet of the Post Office Savings Bank at 31 December 1925, showing depositors' liabilities and assets such as cash, bank accounts and investments.

china-1928:p0401_1.rationale: Balance sheet of the Post Office Savings Bank with depositors' liabilities and investment assets; postal savings fit savings-and-loans.

china-1928:p0403_1.rationale: Key statistics of the Chinese telegraph system: line lengths, instruments, offices and traffic.

china-1928:p0403_2.rationale: Principal telegraph lines with lengths and construction years; quantitative lengths make it statistical.

china-1928:p0404_1.rationale: Telegraph offices and line and cable distances by province for Chinese government telegraphs, 1926.

china-1928:p0406_1.rationale: Inventory of wireless stations with ranges, power and wavelengths; radiotelegraph services. Ownership includes Japanese Army and foreign control, but no explicit imperial-privilege subject is tabulated.

china-1928:p0408_1.rationale: Wireless telegraph stations with ranges, power and wavelengths, by ownership and controller.

china-1928:p0409_1.rationale: Wireless stations in China with range, power, systems and wavelengths; the unreadable cell does not change the quantitative structure.

china-1928:p0410_1.rationale: Summary count of 46 radio stations in China and Hongkong by controlling nation.

china-1928:p0410_2.rationale: Radio stations to be erected by foreign companies for the Chinese Government, with approximate power in kilowatts.

china-1928:p0439_1.rationale: Denominations and subdivisions of Chinese and Turki coinage in Sinkiang; monetary systems fit currency. The content is conversion ratios.
review_questions: Should measurement-and-units apply to coin-equivalence tables?

china-1928:p0471_1.rationale: Counts of modern courts by type and province: judicial organisation.

china-1928:p0472_1.rationale: List of modern prisons by province with opening dates and convict capacity.

china-1928:p0474_1.rationale: Continuation of the list of modern prisons with opening dates, convicts and totals.

china-1928:p0527_1.rationale: Roman Catholic bishops by mission, order, birth year and date of consecration; content is a textual roster with dates only.

china-1928:p0528_1.rationale: Continuation of the roster of Catholic mission bishops with titular sees, birth years and appointment dates; textual.

china-1928:p0530_1.rationale: Catholic missions by region with numbers of bishops and foreign and Chinese priests.

china-1928:p0531_1.rationale: Catholic mission personnel (brothers, nuns, seminarians), Christians, increase and catechumens by mission.

china-1928:p0532_1.rationale: Catholic missions continued, with provinces, bishops and priests by region.
